bug_semantics: A local attacker can supply a truncated/malformed IPv6 capture and run tcprewrite with --fixlen pad. tcpedit_packet derives ip6_hdr from the original packet buffer, then untrunc_packet calls realloc through safe_realloc when pkthdr->len exceeds pkthdr->caplen. If realloc moves the allocation, *pktdata is updated but tcpedit_packet's ip6_hdr alias is not. untrunc_packet returns a positive checksum-recalculation signal, so fix_ipv6_checksums later dereferences the freed IPv6-header alias (the reported read is src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:155 in revision 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a), producing a heap use-after-free and crash.
flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 changed untrunc_packet to receive u_char **pktdata and first introduced `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)` for padding, but it did not refresh the caller's already-derived ip_hdr/ip6_hdr aliases after the possible move. The IPv6 checksum path already existed and continued to pass the stale ip6_hdr after untrunc_packet. Later commit 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only enlarged the realloc request with PACKET_HEADROOM; it did not create the stale-alias mechanism.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object (`git cat-file commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14`) has author and committer `Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>` and message `remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80`; it has no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, bot identity, AI attribution, or any other trailer.
evidence: First-party vulnerability and fix sources: https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/972 reports the IPv6 --fixlen pad path, ASan allocation/free/read stack, revision 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a, and the maintainer's 2025-08-19 statement that 4.5.2-beta3 cannot reproduce it; the same-root-cause report https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/970 identifies realloc in untrunc_packet and the maintainer fix; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/pull/975 says the buffer is already proven large enough and removes realloc; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/releases/tag/v4.5.2 lists #970/#975. Source verification at reported revision: src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:262 calls untrunc_packet with previously derived ip_hdr/ip6_hdr, src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:562 executes safe_realloc, src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:342 passes the unchanged ip6_hdr to fix_ipv6_checksums, and src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:155 dereferences it; src/common/utils.c:66 shows safe_realloc invokes realloc. History verification: `git log -L '/packet = safe_realloc/,+1:src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c'` and `git log -S'packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len'` both trace the statement's first addition to 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14; its one parent is 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e, so it is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a squash requiring decomposition. Direct-parent tree verification: parent src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:243-272 accepts u_char *pktdata and pads it directly with memset at line 271; `git grep` finds no safe_realloc in that parent, while parent src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:85 and src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c:293 prove the IPv6 checksum function/call already existed. The BIC diff adds the realloc and **pktdata handoff without refreshing ip6_hdr, establishing parent absence of the vulnerable mechanism. Version boundaries: the BIC is contained starting at v4.0.5beta1 (and first stable v4.0.5), whereas v4.0.4 predates it; v4.5.1 still contains `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len + PACKET_HEADROOM)` at src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:562. Direct fix https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/commit/73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da deletes that realloc, adds the src/tcprewrite.c MAX_SNAPLEN original-length guard, changes the source version from 4.5.2-beta2 to 4.5.2-beta3, and records `--fixlen use-after-free (#970)` in docs/CHANGELOG. Merge a93ae465b966e6f675b25564ce292fb5cfe762ad lands PR #975. Tag containment shows neither fix commit in v4.5.1/v4.5.2-beta1/v4.5.2-beta2 and both in v4.5.2 and later; the validated clone has no v4.5.2-beta3 tag, but the direct fix itself sets that beta3 version and the maintainer confirms the beta3 behavior in #972. At v4.5.2, the realloc is absent and src/tcprewrite.c:296 contains the new length guard.
reasoning: The vulnerability is created by the interaction of a moving realloc and caller-held interior aliases, not by fix_ipv6_checksums itself. Before the BIC, the same IPv6 checksum call existed, but untrunc_packet could not change the packet allocation; therefore its direct parent lacks this use-after-free mechanism. The BIC is the smallest source commit that made the packet movable during padding while retaining stale ip_hdr/ip6_hdr, and -L/-S history excludes the later PACKET_HEADROOM adjustment as merely a modification. The reported 2024 revision and v4.5.1 retain that lifecycle, while direct commit 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da removes realloc and adds an input-length guard; merge a93ae465b966e6f675b25564ce292fb5cfe762ad lands it for the fixed release boundary. Because the one-parent BIC's exact commit object names a human author/committer and contains no AI/bot/co-author/generated marker, the BIC-only attribution verdict is NOT_AI.
